summary.motive: Punish empty-protection math with a six-man committee so five blockers always face one extra rusher while every receiver is stranded alone in zero man coverage.
summary.keyDefender: MIKE mugged over the A-gap — the free runner up the middle whose arrival coincides exactly with the forced throw
summary.whyItWorks: An empty backfield removes every extra protector and checkdown outlet; six rushers versus five blockers guarantee a free hat, and straight man coverage leaves no soft zone for hot throws to escape into.
summary.failureMode: Quick stick-and-slant throws released on rhythm beat the rush before it lands — if the line slides correctly both ways, the defense has gambled everyone with nobody behind.

beats.title: 1. Six Hats Walk Up Against Empty
beats.text: The offense empties the backfield, and the answer is immediate: Mike mugged over the A-gap at a yard, both edge backers walked to three, safeties creeping. Six potential rushers stand inside eight yards of an unprotectable quarterback.

beats.title: 2. Zero Call: All Six Go
beats.text: No dropper, no exchange, no disguise — every box defender fires his gap at once. The ends slant inside, the edges storm outside, the nose charges between the guards and the mugged Mike shoots behind them.

beats.title: 3. Five Blockers Cannot Match Six
beats.text: The math was settled at the snap: with no back to help, five linemen must handle six rushers moving in four different directions. The interior pinches around the nose while both edges bend toward the quarterback.

beats.title: 4. Hit As He Throws
beats.text: The hot slant comes out on time — and still dies, because zero man means the weak safety is sitting on it with inside leverage while the free-hitting Mike arrives through the A-gap. Pressure and coverage arrive together.

relations.tell: Both safeties AND a linebacker aligned at LOS-level depth against empty — pure zero has nobody deeper than seven yards except the corners.
